rationale: Read the retained receipt of experiment fcb238abc7cd45cdb8b0c03f847b8ad2-experiment (CheckRun 39131804298e4de2bfb8bbb0ccfaf00b, events 13 and 14): the committed configuration entry sits at index 6 while the public configuration future reports index 0 and the documented stat reports "0", so the endpoint question becomes a witnessed violation with a behavior entry. In the same update a repair probe is queued for the parent configuration question: whether an ordinary later configuration entry restores the restarted node's configuration, which bounds how long the empty or stale configuration can persist.

knowledge.statement: The public configuration future reports index 0 and Stats reports latest_configuration_index "0" regardless of the committed configuration entry's index, because the future is built with only the latest configuration set and its latestIndex stays at the zero value.
knowledge.conditions: Any node state; measured after a committed LogConfiguration entry with the live configuration already containing the changed server set.

interpretations.rationale: Current account: both client-facing endpoints are pinned to zero, and the retained execution shows it. Parsed event 13 records a committed LogConfiguration entry at index 6 in a two-peer cluster; parsed event 14, taken in the same state, records future_index 0 with future_index_matches_entry false, stats_latest_configuration_index "0" with stats_index_matches_entry false, and a live configuration that already contains the changed server set (three servers: two voters plus the added nonvoter). Both declared comparisons are violated at index 14. Mechanism from source: GetConfiguration constructs a local configurationsFuture and assigns configurations{latest: r.getLatestConfiguration()}, so committed, committedIndex and latestIndex keep their zero values and ConfigurationFuture.Index() returns 0 even though the IndexFuture contract states that Index holds the index of the applied log entry; Stats maps future.Index() into the documented key latest_configuration_index, so that key is a constant while the neighbouring latest_configuration key shows the real server set. The captured suite only asserts a non-zero Index for an Apply result, so nothing in the snapshot contradicts the reading.
counterevidence: Callers that read only Configuration() are unaffected, and GetConfiguration is documented as returning the latest configuration, which may be uncommitted; the violated contract is the Index exposed by the future and the stat key that copies it.
Internal consumers are unaffected: the main loop still answers configurationsCh with the full configurations struct carrying the real indices, which is what snapshotting uses.
No consensus decision, election, quorum or write outcome depends on this value, so the impact is confined to client-visible reporting.
limitations: Observability-only impact; this is not a safety or liveness defect.
Measured on a two-peer in-memory cluster with the captured test facilities; the same construction is used on every call, so the value does not vary with cluster size, which the probe did not vary.

The comparison uses the configuration entry's own future index as the expected reference; that index is itself produced by the library, and the log-store read of the entry type at that index corroborates it.

scope.description: A two-voter in-memory cluster with commit-tracking stores and RestoreCommittedLogs enabled: the follower is restarted from its own stores so its configuration is empty, then the serving leader commits a new configuration entry (AddNonvoter) and the restarted node's configuration is read before and after that entry arrives.
assumptions: Transports, log stores and FSM are the repository's own InmemTransport, InmemCommitTrackingStore and MockFSM.
Snapshotting is disabled by configuration, so the restarted node has no snapshot and its configuration is empty rather than stale.
The restarted node remains in the serving leader's configuration, so the new configuration entry is replicated to it as a new entry.

experiment.prefix: Start a two-peer cluster with RestoreCommittedLogs and commit-tracking stores; apply five commands; record the follower's configuration and the configuration entry recorded in its log at index 1; shut the follower down and restart it with NewRaft on a fresh transport, then rewire all transports; emit the setup event with the configuration before the restart, the log-recorded configuration and the live configuration length after the restart; commit AddNonvoter on the serving leader; wait until the restarted node reports a non-empty configuration and emit the result event with the change index and type and the repaired configuration.
experiment.requirement: A node that restarted with an empty or stale configuration must regain the configuration in force once the cluster replicates a configuration entry to it.
experiment.responsibility: Raft itself: the node's configuration is loaded by its own recovery and updated by the entries it receives.

comparisons.description: A configuration entry committed after the restart restores the node's configuration to the configuration in force.
